does: Leaves shaped yeast dough in a warm, still place to rise, so that the yeast fills it with gas and it swells and turns light, airy and ready to bake or fry.
how: Shape the dough and set it in a lightly oiled bowl, or on a tray, with room to swell.
Cover it with a damp cloth or oiled film, so that its skin does not dry out.
Leave it somewhere warm and free of draughts until it has roughly doubled, or puffed as the shape asks.
Press a fingertip lightly into it: it is ready when the dent fills back slowly.
Bake or fry it at once, and handle it gently so that the air stays in.

cues.text: The dough has swelled and looks puffy and domed, with small bubbles under the skin.
A fingertip leaves a dent that fills back slowly.
A mild, yeasty, slightly sweet smell, and not a sharp sour one.

mistakes.mistake: Proofing in a spot that is too hot, so that the dough turns sour and loose.
mistakes.fix: Choose a gently warm place and give it more time.

mistakes.mistake: Baking too soon, so that the bread is dense and tight.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the dent fills back slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving it too long, so that it collapses when it is touched or baked.
mistakes.fix: Check it often and bake it as soon as it is ready.

comes_after.why: A dough rises evenly only once it has been worked smooth.
